LESSON: LABORATORY SAFETY

Grade: Grade 7
Subject: INTEGRATED SCIENCE
Strand: Scientific Investigation
Topic 1.2: Laboratory Safety

SECTION 1: WELCOME

• Today’s class: Laboratory Safety
• How we learn: Teach → Worked example → Try this
• Use point notes. Show working. Then take the quiz.
• Big question: What safety measures should be considered while working in the laboratory?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

1. identify common hazards and their symbols in the laboratory
2. explain the causes of common accidents in the laboratory
3. describe First Aid measures for common laboratory accidents
4. appreciate the importance of safety in the laboratory and access to a healthy working environment

SECTION 3: CLASS STUDY (TEACH → EXAMPLE → TRY)

▸ Laboratory Safety

Teach
• Observe Laboratory Safety in real life (school compound, home, farm).
• Use safe examples only.
• Name → explain → apply.

Worked example
• Fact 1 about Laboratory Safety (in pupil words).
• Fact 2 with a Kenyan example.
• Safe action connected to Laboratory Safety.

Try this
• Draw/label one diagram for Laboratory Safety.
• Write 5 bullet facts about Laboratory Safety.
• Say one safety rule.


SECTION: QUICK EXAMPLES

• identify common hazards and their symbols in the laboratory
• explain the causes of common accidents in the laboratory
• describe First Aid measures for common laboratory accidents

SECTION: PRACTICE NOW

1. List 8 facts on Laboratory Safety.
2. Teach a friend using only bullet points.

SECTION: WORK TO DO

1. Revision sheet for Laboratory Safety: meaning, diagram, 5 practice questions.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. What safety measures should be considered while working in the laboratory?

SECTION: REMEMBER

• identify common hazards and their symbols in the laboratory
• explain the causes of common accidents in the laboratory
• describe First Aid measures for common laboratory accidents
• appreciate the importance of safety in the laboratory and access to a healthy working environment

• Next: complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Classroom study notes (Strategy 2)
